description: Averages the waveshape over groups of cyclecnt 'wavecycles' (zero-crossing-delimited segments), replacing each group with repetitions of its mathematical average. The effect is a loss of resolution rather than a blur; large counts approach a sample-hold character. Duration is essentially unchanged (0.1-1.2% drift on noise) but strongly periodic material at high cyclecnt loses the final partial group - see known_issues. Mono only.
musical_use: Mushy, watery degradation and discrete sample-hold effects. Values below 10 keep some semblance of the original with a smeared, underwater cast; around 100 the sound freezes into stepped 'sample hold' blocks. For modest distortion stay at 5 or less. A time-varying cyclecnt (breakpoint file) can slide a sound from intact to frozen across its length - the binary accepts this even though its own usage banner is silent about it.

cyclecnt.description: Number of wavecycles over which to average (integer; CDP-enforced range 2-32767 - the binary rejects 1 with 'Value (1.000000) out of range (2.000000 to 32767.000000)'). Values <10 retain the source's character, ~100 gives sample-hold; 5 or less for modest distortion. Runtime-limited by content: a value exceeding the file's wavecycle count aborts with 'source sound too short to attempt this process.'. May vary over time (manual-confirmed; probe verified - a 3->40 breakpoint render differs from both endpoint scalar renders).

maxwavelen.description: Maximum permissible wavelength in seconds (CDP's internal default is 0.50; enforced range at 44.1 kHz was 0.000363 to 1.0 - the lower bound is sample-rate-dependent). Segments longer than this (e.g. long near-silences between zero crossings) are not treated as wavecycles. Scalar only - a breakpoint file is refused.

skipcycles.description: Number of wavecycles to skip at the start of the file (integer; CDP-enforced range 0-32767; internal default 0). As with distort repeat, skipped material is dropped from the output entirely (verified: -s100 on a 440 Hz tone shortened the output by ~100/440 s), so nonzero values make the static duration model over-predict. Scalar only - a breakpoint file is refused.

examples.expected_use: Watery, slightly degraded version of the source; duration unchanged.
Stepped, frozen blocks of waveshape; on strongly pitched sources expect the output a few percent shorter (final partial group dropped).

known_issues: DIVERGENCE: the usage banner says nothing about time-varying cyclecnt, but the HTML manual states 'cyclecnt may vary over time' and the binary accepts a breakpoint file (exit 0; output differs from both endpoint scalar renders). Same banner-silent/breakpoint-capable pattern as distort multiply, with manual and binary agreeing this time.

The static duration model degrades on strongly periodic material at high cyclecnt: the final partial group (up to cyclecnt wavecycles) is dropped, e.g. -9.3% at cyclecnt 100 on a 2 s 440 Hz tone (1.8141 s), -2.5% at cyclecnt 20. On noise inputs drift stayed within 0.1-1.2% (cyclecnt 5-100), and output can come out slightly LONGER (+0.57% observed) because averaged wavelengths are re-quantised.
skipcycles drops the skipped wavecycles from the output rather than passing them through; the shortfall is content-dependent (cycles, not seconds) and is excluded from the duration model.
Mono only: a stereo input is refused with 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255).
